correctness.rationale: Tight-edge incidence rank plus bipartition parity make all surviving graph edges tight at each polar vertex. Every removed matched pair has graph distance three and a potential difference of magnitude either 1 or 3; if all are 1, extension to K_{p,q} forces the classical constant-one-part binary families of sizes 2^p and 2^q with two common functions. If a deleted pair x_i,y_i has a gap three, its endpoints can be set to 0,3; each remaining cross edge forces all other X heights 2 and Y heights 1 (p,q>=3), generating exactly two signed exceptional facets for that pair and excluding simultaneous other gaps. The group preserves the two parts or swaps them when p=q, permuting matched and unmatched members separately. In each binary family counts (j,l) are identified only with (k-j,s-k-l), and Burnside plus the shared constant and exceptional orbits gives the displayed formula and binomial orbit sizes. An independently written spanning-tree enumerator verified (p,q,k)=(3,3,0),(3,3,3),(3,4,2),(4,5,3),(5,5,5), with total facets 14,20,26,52,72 and exception counts 0,6,4,6,10; no finite bound was mistaken for universal proof.

originality.rationale: The complete bipartite k=0 formula and its two constant-family normals belong to Higashitani–Jochemko–Michałek; the balanced fully deleted crown special case has known diameter-three gap patterns and some facet geometry. The asserted additional object is the all-(p,q,k) rectangular partial-deletion rigidity, exact per-edge additivity and full sign/automorphism orbit multiplicities, not those prior corner cases.
residual_risks: The crown p=q=k case has prior coverage and is not independently novel; some other covered small examples may appear in existing tables.
